question: A project manager has received a draft board paper and has time to review it properly. In what order should she carry out her review?
options: A) Confirm every requested topic is covered; check the claims that carry the argument; correct the tone and formatting; approve it.
B) Check the claims that carry the argument; correct the tone and formatting; approve it; confirm every requested topic is covered.
C) Correct the tone and formatting; check the claims that carry the argument; confirm every requested topic is covered; approve it.
D) Approve it; confirm every requested topic is covered; correct the tone and formatting; check the claims that carry the argument.
correct_answers: A) Confirm every requested topic is covered; check the claims that carry the argument; correct the tone and formatting; approve it.
explanations: Correct. Coverage is settled first because it determines what there is to check, accuracy is then established on the full set of content, and presentation is polished last on text that is staying. Approval comes only after all three.
Verifying claims before knowing what is missing means the added sections arrive later, unchecked, and after approval in this ordering.
Polishing first means investing effort in wording that may be deleted once a missing topic is added or an unsupported claim is removed.
Approving before any review has happened makes the remaining steps a formality, and anything found afterwards has already been signed off.
